name: desire for order
quote: A place for everything, everything in its place.
description: Wanting the relationship between things to follow a pattern that allows you to understand how to interact with them.
perceptions: There's a way things should be.
If things are following this pattern, it's easier to predict and influence them.

guidance.description: If a desire for order is negatively affecting your life and relationships, you might have a form of OCD.

variations.name: desire for social order
variations.description: Wanting people to behave within expected guidelines.
perceptions: It's better if people follow the rules.
results: If people don't behave within particular guidelines, you're likely to perceive the results in a negative way.
Want to find a way to get that person to behave as expected.

guidance.description: On a near-daily basis, we’re faced with situations that we know are wrong, but saying something might make us or others feel uncomfortable.

variations.name: desire for predictability
variations.description: Wanting to have and confirm a repeatable internal model of something or someone.
perceptions: I know how to handle someone or something that reacts the same way in a given situation.
results: If something or someone is not acting in a predictable way, it may result in confusion or frustration.

comparisons.description: Being predictable doesn't mean it's simple, well-ordered, or positive. But it's better to have a complicated memorized system than none at all. For example, I might know where every book on my shelf is from memory. For me it's predictable and easy to find a given book. My brain considers this 'functional order'. But if there's no system discernible to others, they would not consider my books structurally ordered.

examples: Preference for formulaic music or fiction.
Preference for chain restaurants where you know what you're getting.

variations.name: desire for simplicity
variations.description: Wanting the relationship between things to follow a basic pattern that allows you to easily understand how to interact with them.
perceptions: I can easily understand how to interact with these things.
results: If something or someone is not acting in a simple easy-to-understand way, it may result in confusion or frustration.

comparisons.description: Being 'ordered' does not mean it's simple. For instance, the Periodic Table of Elements is ordered but takes some work to understand. If you don't see the order in something, you may wish it were simpler.

guidance.description: We live in a complicated world. These articles describe the benefits of simplifying your environment.
We have a tendency to want to over-simplify things as a form of wishful thinking. These articles suggest there are downsides to coddling your brain that you should be aware of.

examples: Cutting unnecessary things out of your schedule.

variations.name: desire for clean living
variations.description: Wanting for a critical characteristic of an environment that affects your physical, social, or existential health to meet a very strict standard.
perceptions: It's critical that my environment adhere to a certain rule.
If this pattern is broken, disgusting things may happen.
desires: desire to be perceived a certain way

comparisons.description: Being 'ordered' does not mean something is 'clean' pr 'pure'. For example, things in your home may be well-ordered but dusty.

guidance.description: Many people are worried about poisoning themselves with bad food, misinformation, or toxic chemicals.
If you feel that anxiety about purity has become too much, you may consider researching whether this an unhealthy obsession.

comparisons.description: We want to understand how each environment is ordered so that we can predict what might happen in various scenarios and influence the outcome. In short, the desire for agency drives a desire for order, which drives us to put energy into gaining knowledge about the environment and perhaps trying to improve it.

commentaries.quote: Many of us have ideals that we work hard to live up to. Sometimes we can become obsessive about aligning with an ideal as a way of hoping to control negative things in our lives.
If things seem disordered and you can't align them, it may be that the expectations are not quite right.
There is a way to improve the chance of having accurate expectations. It's called the Scientific Method.

There's a lot of overlap underlying our desires for social status, purity, safety, and comfort. It may be worth considering whether the strength of these desires is helping you or causing unnecessary stress.
Good order is the foundation of all great things.

To put the world in order, we must first put the nation in order; to put the nation in order, we must put the family in order; to put the family in order, we must cultivate our personal life; and to cultivate our personal life, we must first set our hearts right.
The art of progress is to preserve order amid change and to preserve change amid order.
The mind cannot support moral chaos for long. Men are under as strong a compulsion to invent an ethical setting for their behavior as spiders are to weave themselves webs.
